players.note: Bucky Irving is the RB15 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.7 touches and 90.8 total yards. He has a 63.8% snap rate, 57.1% of the rushing work, a 47.6% route share, and a 10.7% target share. Among 42 qualifying backs, Irving is 30th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Irving should have another strong stat line this week. Across their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the ninth-highest rushing success rate, the second-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest gap rushing success rate (Irving: 53.3% gap).

Chase Brown has had such a poor run out this season as the RB20 in fantasy points per game. He has one touchdown this season and is the RB12 in expected fantasy points per game. Overall, he has averaged 18.4 touches and 71.3 total yards. He has been splitting the early-down work with Samaje Perine over the last two games, while last week his snap rate jumped back to 74.5% as he also had a 59.4% route share (16.7% target share). Over the last two games, he has had a 55% rushing share while splitting the red zone work with Perine evenly (both backs have two red zone rushing attempts). This is despite Brown having a 70% snap share during that span inside the 20-yard line. Among 42 qualifying backs, Brown is 25th in yards after contact per attempt and 32nd in missed tackle rate, but his offensive line has done him no favors as he is also 33rd in yards before contact per attempt. This could be the "get right" game for Brown. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards before contact per attempt.

Last week, in his first game back, Josh Jacobs was the RB7 in fantasy scoring. He played 53.8% of the snaps with 57.9% of the rushing workload, a 43.5% route share, and a 15.6% target share. Jacobs had an 11.1% explosive run rate, 1.45 yards after contact per attempt, and a 9% missed tackle rate. Those aren't amazing numbers (outside of the explosive run rate), but it's a one-game sample, so I'm not freaking out. Jacobs finished with 16 touches and 91 total yards. It was a more substantial workload than I thought he'd get in his first game back, but five of those touches were receptions. His 11 carries were about what I thought he would see. Jacobs should have another strong game this week. Since Week 3, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt.

Tetairoa McMillan is the WR13 in fantasy points per game. In the four games he has played with Jalen Coker as a full-time player, McMillan has had a 21.5% target share with 2.19 YPRR, four red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 27.9% first-read share. This week McMillan faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four games with Coker as a full-go, McMillan has had a 21% TPRR and 2.67 YPRR against two high. McMillan has a nice shot at a bounce-back game this week against a Green Bay secondary that (since Week 3) has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

George Pickens is the WR24 in fantasy points per game with at least 15 PPR points in two of his last three games. I'm projecting a milder stat line this week for Pickens. Yes, you guessed it. Arizona is a two-high, heavy pass defense. Pickens has a 20.5% target share with 2.00 YPRR, six red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 23.1% first-read share. Arizona has the highest two-high rate in the NFL (70.5%). Against two high, Pickens' TPRR drops off a map from 35% (against single high) to 17%, and his YPRR falls from 2.92 to 1.51. Working in his favor is the fact that Arizona has been horrible at defending perimeter wide receivers, which could help counteract Pickens' coverage woes. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Pickens could still be a decent WR2 this week, but this doesn't look like a blow-up spot.

Jalen Coker didn't have the massive game last week that I was projecting, as Carolina's passing offense cratered as Bryce Young fell back to Earth. Coker could have a bounce-back outing this week. In his four full games this season, Coker has had a 22.2% target share with 2.40 YPRR, five red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 30.2% first-read share. Overall, he is the WR22 in fantasy points per game. This week, Coker faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four full games, against two-high, Coker has had a 23% TPRR with 1.85 YPRR. Bryce Young will have to look like his early-season form for this passing attack to have bite again, but it's possible. Since Week 3, Green Bay has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

Garrett Wilson is the WR22 in fantasy points per game, but he has had fewer than nine PPR points in three of his last four games. With that said, Wilson could get the squeaky wheel treatment this week. Overall, Wilson still has a 25.1% target share with 2.09 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 30.6% first-read share. His quiet Week 6 performance is easily explainable, as he had to deal with Christian Gonzalez on 93.9% of his routes. The Raiders don't have a corner in that talent area code on their depth chart. In their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the fifth-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

D'Andre Swift is the RB12 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19.7 touches and 89.7 total yards. Swift has had a 60.4% snap rate, 47.2% of the rushing work, a 38.8% route share, and a 10.4% target share. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Swift is 19th in yards after contact per attempt and seventh in missed tackle rate. He'll have to lean on his volume and touchdown equity this week against an elite Seattle run defense. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Michael Wilson has been struggling recently. Wilson is still the WR32 in fantasy points per game, but he hasn't managed more than 12 PPR points since Marvin Harrison Jr.'s departure from Arizona. Since Week 5, he has had a 16% target share with 1.01 YPRR, three red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 17.8% first-read share. He hasn't finished with more than 55 receiving yards in any of these three games. I think he can break out of his funk this week. Dallas has the third-highest single-high rate in the NFL (71.1%). Wilson has crushed single-high this season with a 31% TPRR and 2.03 YPRR. Joey Porter Jr. hasn't been shadowing in Dallas, so I don't expect him to this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Rhamondre Stevenson is the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 13.9 touches and 69.8 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Stevenson is 16th in missed tackle rate and 24th in yards after contact per attempt. Stevenson is a strong RB2 again this week. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt, the seventh-highest gap yards per carry, and the sixth-highest gap rushing success rate (Stevenson: 68.8% gap).

Luther Burden is the WR24 in fantasy points per game and looks electric any time he touches the ball. Luther Burden's route share dipped to 41.5% in Week 6, but he was back up at 66.7% last week. Overall, Burden has a 19.5% target share, 2.70 YPRR, nine red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. This week, he'll face a Seattle pass defense that has the seventh-highest two-high rate in the NFL (60.2%). Against two-high, Burden has a 25% TPRR and 3.07 YPRR. Those numbers are incredibly strong. Burden has a nasty matchup this week, but he also has the talent to walk away with a solid stat line this week despite it. Across their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Tony Pollard was a fantasy point scoring behemoth last week as the RB1 overall in fantasy. Pollard finished with 28 touches, 155 total yards, and three scores. It was an insane performance. Since Week 2, Pollard has averaged 19.2 touches and 82.3 total yards. Over the last two games, his playing time has increased with a 74.8% snap rate, 83% of the rushing workload, and a 37.5% route share (5.7% target share). Pollard has been running strong this season. Among 42 qualifying backs, Pollard is 16th in explosive run rate and tenth in yards after contact per attempt. He could have another nice stat line this week. Across their last five games, Cincy has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the fourth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 12th-most yards after contact per attempt. Pollard is an RB2 with upside.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB12 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.3 touches and 97 total yards. Gordon has been outstanding. I didn't see this coming, but I'm so happy to see him excelling. Among 42 qualifying backs, Gordon is fourth in explosive run rate, 15th in yards after contact per attempt, and 18th in missed tackle rate. Gordon should have another strong showing this week. In their last five games, New England has allowed the sixth-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.

DJ Moore (shoulder) practiced on a limited basis all week. He has been listed as questionable, but he is expected to play this week. In his two full games this season, Moore has had a 30.9% target share, 3.63 YPRR, 0.174 FD/RR, and a 33.3% first-read share. In those two contests, he racked up two red zone targets and four deep targets. No matter how you slice it, that's elite usage for a wide receiver. Moore is a strong WR2 this week with WR1 upside. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the third-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Stefon Diggs will be leading the way for Washington's aerial attack moving forward. Diggs is the WR24 in fantasy points per game with a 20.9% target share, 1.60 YPRR, five red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 25.4% first-read share. Diggs should be a strong WR2 this week. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the 13th-most yards per target, the most receiving fantasy points per game, and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Every time I think DK Metcalf should smash, he turns in a wet fart stat line. Metcalf started hot with 56 receiving yards in the first half last week before falling asleep after halftime. Metcalf is the WR36 in fantasy points per game, with four games this season with fewer than nine PPR points. Metcalf has a 21.9% target share with 1.41 YPRR, four red zone targets, 14 deep targets, and a 31.7% first-read share. This week, he faces a Browns pass defense that has the highest single high rate in the NFL (75.2%). Against single high, Metcalf's TPRR has risen from 20% to 23%, and his YPRR has increased from 1.11 to 1.56. The coverage structure is in his favor, but Cleveland has been shutting down perimeter wide receivers. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Breece Hall could retake his commanding lead role this week, but I also could see Braelon Allen mixing in more, and this backfield being more of a committee. Allen was so good while Hall was out it might be tough for Aaron Glenn to put that genie back in the backup bottle. In Weeks 1-2, Hall had a 61.7% snap rate while averaging 22.5 touches and 104.8 total yards. Hall hasn't been amazing on a per-touch basis this season with only 1.49 yards after contact per attempt and a 14% missed tackle rate. I'm sure those numbers won't look better this week with Hall coming off an injury, but I could be wrong. The Raiders could also help improve those efficiency numbers. Their run defense has been horrible over their last five games, allowing the third-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the highest yards before contact per attempt, and the third-highest missed tackle rate.

In his first start before the bye week, Rachaad White finished with 11 touches and 57 total yards as the RB10 for the week. White played 70.5% of the snaps with 41.2% of the rushing work and a 51.1% route share (12.5% target share). I expect White to see a similar workload this week. White is a volume play only. His per-touch efficiency has been decent with 2.06 yards after contact per attempt and a 17% missed tackle rate. White should have a decent outing. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the tenth-highest rushing success rate, the ninth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the fifth-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the third-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 5, Germie Bernard has been the WR23 in fantasy points per game with a 22.7% target share, 1.92 YPRR (4.8 aDOT), four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 21.4% first-read share. He has essentially been Pittsburgh's Rashee Rice with a 24% designed target share. This week, he faces a Browns pass defense that has the highest single high rate in the NFL (75.2%). Against single high, since Week 5, Bernard has had a 19% TPRR and 2.05 YPRR. Bernard has a solid matchup this week and could have a bounce-back game after a quiet outing against the Saints. Across their last five games, the Browns have allowed the 12th-most yards per target to slot receivers while ranking 19th in fantasy points per opportunity.

Over the last two games, with Tanner McKee under center, Dallas Goedert has been the TE14 and TE16 in weekly scoring. Goedert has had an 18.8% target share with 1.85 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 25% first-read share. Goedert is a solid TE1 this week. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the eighth-most yards per target, the seventh-most receiving yards, and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Quinshon Judkins is the RB19 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.2 touches and 71.1 total yards. He has a 59.2% snap rate, 58.1% of the rushing work, and a 30.3% route share (11.4% target share). His per-touch efficiency has been horrible with only 1.80 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Judkins will need a touchdown and all the volume he can handle this week to produce a nice stat line for fantasy purposes. Over the last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-lowest explosive run rate, the fourth-lowest rushing success rate, and the fifth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Well, I hoped KC Concepcion would have his breakout game last week, and it happened. Concepcion was the WR8 in weekly scoring. That pulls him up to WR51 in fantasy points per game for the season. I know, not great. He has a 20.5% target share with 1.73 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 27.1% first-read share. It's possible Concepcion keeps the train rolling this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 11th-most fantasy points per game to slot receivers.

Hello, Omar Cooper Jr. I'm sorry for doubting you last week. Over the last two games, Cooper has been the WR6 and WR9 in weekly scoring. In those games, Cooper had a 20% target share, 4.45 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 29.3% first-read share. Cooper could have another fantastic game in Week 8. In their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the fourth-most receiving fantasy points per game, the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity, and the most receiving touchdowns (tied) to slot receivers.

Over the last two weeks, with Caleb Williams back, Colston Loveland has been the TE4 and TE3 in weekly scoring. In those two games, Loveland has had a 26.1% target share with 2.39 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 31.7% first-read share. He has been ELITE! This was exactly who we thought we were drafting this summer. Like Luther Burden, Loveland has a tough mountain to climb this week, but he could still succeed despite the horrible matchup. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the second-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Just note that Trey McBride did post 18.1 fantasy points against this defense in Week 2.

T.J. Hockenson is having a resurgent season as the TE9 in fantasy points per game. Among 42 qualifying tight ends, Hockenson is sixth in target share (18.9%), sixth in YPRR (2.14), ninth in red zone targets (six), and ninth in first-read share (19.8%). Hockenson is headed toward another TE1 week against Detroit. Over their last five games, Hockenson's former team has allowed the fifth-most yards per target to tight ends, the second-most fantasy points per opportunity, and the most receiving touchdowns to tight ends.

Well, damn. Ok, I guess it's time to start believing in Tre Tucker. Tucker has three weeks with at least 21 PPR points this season as the WR20 in fantasy points per game. Tucker has a 17.7% target share with 2.18 YPRR, six red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 23.3% first-read share. Tucker could keep the party bus rolling in Week 8. In their last five games, the Jets have allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Travis Kelce continues to hum along as a TE1. Kelce is the TE7 in fantasy points per game with a 17.8% target share, 2.23 YPRR, three red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.2% first-read share. Kelce has also posted a STRONG 0.117 FD/RR. Kelce could easily post another TE1 finish this week as he leads the Chiefs in targets. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Ok, Jamo...I'm sorry. I was down on Jamo last week, and he made me pay for it. Jameson Williams is the WR25 in fantasy points per game after the big game. Williams has a 16.6% target share with 1.75 YPRR, seven red zone targets, ten deep targets (eighth among wideouts), and a 23.4% first-read share. After last week, Williams' numbers against two high look much better, which will help him this week. Minnesota has the fourth-highest two-high rate (63.3%). Against two-high, Williams has a 19% TPRR (second on the team) and 1.81 YPRR. Jared Goff will be blitzed into oblivion this week, and Williams should be a trusted weapon on those plays. Williams has a 19% TPRR and 2.04 when Goff has been blitzed. It's a tough matchup for Williams, so consider him a volatile player this week as usual. Over their last five games, Minny has allowed the third-fewest yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Before Buffalo's bye, Dalton Kincaid bounced back (some) with his first game with at least double-digit PPR points since Week 2. Kincaid is the TE11 in fantasy points per game. Really, it's off the strength of those opening two games of the season. Kincaid has a 61.5% route share, a 17% target share, 2.56 YPRR, five red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 21.2% first-read share. It's possible that Kincaid has a solid game this week, but the coverage structure isn't in his favor. Baltimore has the fifth-highest rate of two-high (62.4%). Against two-high, Kincaid's TPRR has fallen to 19%, and his YPRR sits at 1.23. Across their last five games, Baltimore is 18th in yards per target allowed to tight ends while surrendering the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Kincaid has a wide range of outcomes this week.

Denzel Boston has dropped to the WR34 after two quiet weeks. Over the last two games, he has scored only 8.2 PPR points combined. Overall, he has a 19% target share with 1.68 YPRR, five red zone targets, 14 deep targets, and a 22.9% first-read share. Unfortunately, it looks like Boston is headed toward another quieter day. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity against the position.

Ok, let's start this off with A.J. Brown isn't fully healthy. I don't care what New England says. Brown doesn't pass the eye test. Since his return to the lineup, he has been the WR60 and WR35 in weekly scoring. In those two games, Brown had a 23.8% target share, 1.17 YPRR, three red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 39.5% first-read share. Maybe this is the breakout game, but I worry about that actually happening in Week 8. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Brown has a wide range of outcomes this week. Brown is also dealing with a knee issue now. His problematic knee flared up this week. He didn't practice Thursday or Friday and has been listed as questionable. Have a backup plan for Brown this week. He could easily miss Week 8.

Jordan Mason will lead the backfield again this week. Aaron Jones sustained a knee injury during the fourth quarter of last week's game, but Mason was the lead back in the first three quarters of action. Last week, in those three quarters, Mason had a 55% snap rate, 12 opportunities, and a 42.9% route share (10.5% target share). He also had the only red zone carry during that span for the backfield. With his limited work this season, Mason hasn't been efficient with only 1.97 yards after contact per attempt and a 3% missed tackle rate. I don't have high hopes for Mason this week, but if he gets in the end zone, he could be a decent flex. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the fifth-highest explosive run rate, the tenth-highest rushing success rate, and the sixth-most yards before contact per attempt.

Keenan Allen has been producing. Across his last four games, Allen has finished as the WR20, WR35, WR17, and WR44 in weekly scoring. Since Week 3, he has led the team with a 22.2% target share and 25.7% first-read share while posting 1.94 YPRR with three red zone targets and two deep targets. Allen could be a strong flex again this week. Across their last five games, the Jags have given up the fourth-most yards per target and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

It looks like Ladd McConkey will be back this week after sustaining a concussion in Week 6. McConkey has been in and out of the lineup all season with the concussion, a rib issue, a foot issue, and a chest injury. When he has been on the field, he has had a 20% TPRR, 2.22 YPRR, and a 14.1% first-read share. It's tough to consider him as anything more than a dart-throw flex at this point in the season with a bad matchup. Over their last five games, the Rams have allowed the second-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Jeremiyah Love (ankle) had limited practices this week before upgrading to a full session on Friday. He'll be back this week. He doesn't have an injury designation this week. I expect Love to share the backfield workload this week with Tyler Allgeier. In Weeks 1-2 and 4-5, Love averaged 13 touches and 43.2 total yards while playing 45.1% of the snaps with a 48.4% rushing share and a 25.2% route share (5.4% target share). Playing through an ankle issue, Love posted 2.03 yards after contact per attempt and a 15% missed tackle rate. Those are solid stats in their own right, but especially when you consider he was running on one healthy leg. Love could have a nice day even with Allgeier leeching work. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Since Week 4, Hunter Henry has been the TE9 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 4, Henry has had a 15.7% target share, 2.30 YPRR, four red zone targets, and a 14.8% first-read share. Henry could be a TE1 again this week as Miami has been unable to stop tight ends. Across their last five games, Miami has allowed the most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Well, it happened. Makai Lemon had his best game of the season against a horrible Dallas secondary. Lemon was the WR13 for the week. Over the last two weeks, Lemon has had a 16.3% target share with 1.13 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 21.4% first-read share. Lemon offers some flex upside this week with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks out. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers while ranking 16th in yards per target allowed to the position.

Well, I was all in on Malik Washington, and he had arguably his worst game of the season. Overall, Washington is the WR42 in fantasy points per game. Last week, with Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas active, Washington ran 60% of his routes from the slot. Overall, Washington has had a 25.8% target share with 1.85 YPRR, two red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 28.1% first-read share. Since Week 6, New England has had the third-highest single-high rate (66.7%). This season, against single high, Washington has had a 22% TPRR and 1.85 YPRR. Washington could have a bounce-back game this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the third-most yards per target and the second-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Braelon Allen might have been too good while Breece Hall was out for New York to stick him back into a change-of-pace role. In Weeks 4-7, Allen averaged 20.8 touches and 105.3 total yards as the RB22 in fantasy points per game. Allen has shown per-touch efficiency this season that I didn't know he was capable of, with a STRONG 15.7% explosive run rate, 2.79 yards after contact per attempt, and a 22% missed tackle rate. If the Jets decide to open the game by mixing both backs in and go with a hot hand approach, don't be surprised if Allen's hands look like they touched the sun. The Raiders' run defense has been wretched. Over their last five games, they have allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the highest yards before contact per attempt, and the third-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 4, Kyle Pitts has been the TE6 in fantasy points per game. During that stretch, he has had a 17.2% target share, 2.09 YPRR, six red zone targets, and a 19.3% first-read share. Last week, I was low on Pitts because the 49ers had been tough against tight ends and the coverage structure didn't align with Pitts' usage for the season. Atlanta did change his usage last week against single high, as he had a 27% TPRR against the coverage structure. It's possible he could see that type of usage again this week against a single high heavy Tampa Bay pass defense. Tampa Bay has the fourth-highest single-high rate in the NFL (60.4%). Tampa Bay has allowed solid production to tight ends in their last five games, surrendering the 14th-most yards per target and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. It also doesn't hurt that Pitts annihilated the Bucs last year, finishing as the TE7 and TE1 in weekly scoring against them in their two meetings.

Since Week 5, Blake Corum has been the RB9 in fantasy points per game. Over the last three weeks, Corum has had a 32.7% snap rate, 38.3% of the rushing attempts, and a 12.4% route share (6% target share). During this stretch, Corum has averaged 12.3 touches and 77.6 total yards with three scores. Corum has been electric on a per-touch basis. Among 42 qualifying backs, Corum is ninth in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate. He should run wild again this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the 14th-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest gap yards per carry (Corum: 54.7% gap).

Jordan Addison has been almost non-existent this season, as the WR65 in fantasy points per game. Addison has a 17.9% target share with 1.25 YPRR, one red zone target, five deep targets, and a 24.1% first-read share. Addison has failed to surpass 60 receiving yards in all but one game this season. Addison could double that output after this week. Detroit has the eighth-highest rate of single-high (56.9%). Against single-high, Addison's usage has gone up, with this TPRR rising from 12% to 21% and his YPRR jumping from 0.78 (against two-high) to 1.77. Now, Detroit has tightened up its defense against perimeter receivers over the last five games, allowing the 11th-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity, which leaves Addison as a middle-of-the-road flex.

Jaylen Waddle opened this week (chest) with a DNP. He managed limited practice sessions on Thursday and Friday. He has been listed as questionable. I could easily see him being ruled out Sunday before kickoff, so monitor the news all day and be prepared with a backup option if you're looking to start him. I'm leaning toward sitting him this week, even if he is active, though. Waddle has been crushed by Bo Nix before this injury occurred. He is the WR48 in fantasy points per game. Waddle has a 19.7% target share with 1.56 YPRR, three red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 29% first-read share. He has a horrible matchup this week. Across their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Josh Downs has been slumping. I'm not laying this at the feet of Downs. It's a Daniel Jones problem. Downs hasn't had more than 50 receiving yards in a game since Week 3. Over the last four games, Downs hasn't finished higher than WR41 in any game. Since Week 4, Downs has had a 13.4% target share with 0.86 YPRR, one red zone target, four deep targets, and a 17% first-read share. Indy would be wise to feature him this week to drive his trade stock up, but we'll see if that happens. Downs is flex-viable again this week. In their last five games, Jacksonville has allowed the ninth-most yards per target to slot receivers while ranking 17th in fantasy points per opportunity.

Brenton Strange is quietly the TE12 in fantasy points per game. He's having a strong season with a 17.9% target share, 2.02 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 19.5% first-read share. I'd love it if the Jags started feeding him more high-cholesterol usage downfield near the goal line. Despite those factors lacking, Strange could easily be a TE1 again this week. Indy has the 12th-highest single-high rate (52.1%). Against single-high, Strange is second on the team with a 30% TPRR while posting 2.82 YPRR. Over the last five games, Indy has faced the second-fewest tight end targets, but they have given up the sixth-most receiving touchdowns (tied) and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position during that span. The Jags could lean on Strange even more this week with Jakobi Meyers dinged up.Â

While I think Luther Burden can overcome a horrible matchup, I don't share the same optimism for Rome Odunze this week. Odunze is the WR55 in fantasy points per game with a 15.4% target share with 1.70 YPRR, five red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 17.6% first-read share. Across their last five games, Seattle has allowed the tenth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game and the 14th-fewest yards per target to perimeter wide receivers. Sit Odunze this week.

Jakobi Meyers is the WR37 in fantasy points per game with three top-36 weekly finishes (WR28, WR17, WR27). Meyers has a 15.2% target share with 1.85 YPRR, six red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 17.3% first-read share. He has quietly taken a step back and become the third option in the passing game this season behind Parker Washington and Brenton Strange. This week, he could easily post a strong flex-worthy stat line. Indy has the 12th-highest single-high rate (52.1%). Against single-high, Meyers has a 17% TPRR and 2.02 YPRR. Meyers could succeed this week, but it's not an easy matchup. Across their last five games, Indy has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the ninth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Meyers is dealing with ankle and hamstring issues. He practiced on a limited basis before missing Friday's practice. He has been listed as questionable. I hate late week downgrades. Monitor the news. I could see Meyers getting ruled out this weekend.

Wan'Dale Robinson is the WR54 in fantasy points per game with three outings this season with at least 11 PPR points. With Carnell Tate out, Robinson will operate as Tennessee's WR1. He's in a great spot to capitalize on the bump in role this week. DJ Turner isn't moving to nickel full time, so Robinson should have a nice matchup. Robinson has a 20.2% target share with 1.15 YPRR, eight red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 25.9% first-read share. His FD/RR is a solid 0.084. Cincy has been bleeding out production to slot receivers. Across their last five games, Cincy has allowed the fifth-most yards per target, the most fantasy points per opportunity, and the most receiving touchdowns (tied) to slot receivers.

Xavier Worthy is having another forgettable season as the WR53 in fantasy points per game. He has scored at least 11 PPR points this season only three times. Worthy has an 18.3% target share with 1.25 YPRR, four red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 25.6% first-read share. Worthy is a sit again this week. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity while ranking 15th in receiving fantasy points per game against perimeter wide receivers.

Chris Godwin hasn't been fantasy relevant all year as the WR64 in fantasy points per game. He has yet to post even double-digit PPR points. Godwin has a 16.6% target share, 1.18 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 19.3% first-read share. It's been tough to watch. Godwin is a sit-and-droppable at this point. Across their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Last week, as Sean Payton talked about having Jonah Coleman on a snap count in his return, Coleman led the backfield in snaps (50%), rushing attempts (nine, 34.6%), and was second in route share (21.9%), running one less route than RJ Harvey. Coleman finished with 11 touches and 69 total yards. This season, with his 19 carries, he has a wonderful 23.5% explosive run rate and 52.6% success rate, while his 1.69 yards after contact per attempt and 11% missed tackle rate aren't anything to write home about. Coleman is a low-end flex this week because his role is still in flux and the matchup is horrible. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Harold Fannin Jr. is the TE17 in fantasy points per game. Fannin has had fewer than two PPR points in two of his last three games. Overall, he has a 17.1% target share with 1.28 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 16.7% first-read share. Fannin could pop back up with a TE1 week against the Steelers. Across their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Rico Dowdle was the RB22, finishing with 15 touches and 86 total yards. Dowdle played 44.4% of the snaps with 30% of the rushing attempts and a 55.9% route share (20% target share). Dowdle has a decent 2.06 yards after contact per attempt and a 10% missed tackle rate. Dowdle could post another strong week against the Browns' porous run defense. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, in his return to the lineup, Caleb Douglas secured two of his three targets with 70 receiving yards and two scores. Douglas had a 67.9% route share, a 14.3% target share, one red zone target, and a 16.7% first-read share. Christian Gonzalez could shadow either Caleb Douglas this week. It's also possible that doesn't happen. Last week, Gonzalez only followed Rome Odunze on 40.5% of his routes. Since Week 6, New England has had the third-highest single high rate (66.7%). This season, against single high, Douglas has had a 20% TPRR with 1.96 YPRR. If Douglas doesn't get shadowed by Christian Gonzalez this week, he could have another strong showing. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Ryan Flournoy has replaced Jake Ferguson as the third wheel in the Dallas passing attack. Since Week 5, Flournoy has had a 13.8% target share, 1.96 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 12.2% first-read share. Arizona has the highest two-high rate in the NFL (70.5%). Since Week 5, against two-high, Flournoy has seen his TPRR increase from 14% to 18% while posting 1.78 YPRR. Flournoy is a solid flex option this week. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Khalil Shakir might be the WR45 in fantasy points per game, but in his last three games, he has had at least 11 PPR points in each game. In those three games, Shakir has had an 18.8% target share with 2.68 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 24.1% first-read share. Baltimore has the fifth-highest rate of two-high (62.4%). Against two-high, Shakir has a 21% TPRR and 2.07 YPRR. Shakir is a strong flex this week against a Baltimore pass defense that, across their last five games, has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers. DJ Moore's return could hinder Shakir's ceiling this week, but he should still return a nice stat line.

Mike McDaniel has capsized Omarion Hampton as the RB31 in fantasy points per game. Hampton has averaged 14.8 touches and 57.5 total yards. In the Bolts dumpster fire backfield, Hampton has had a 45.6% snap rate, 47.3% of the rushing work, and a 22.6% route share (5% target share). Among 42 qualifying backs, Hampton is ninth in yards after contact per attempt and 28th in missed tackle rate. Hampton is just a touchdown-dependent flex again this week. The Rams have slowly tightened up their run defense to league average standards. Over their last five games, they have been 15th in explosive run rate, 14th in rushing success rate, and have allowed the 12th-lowest missed tackle rate.

In his last two games, before the bye week, Chig Okonkwo was the TE15 and TE11 in weekly scoring. In those games, he had a 72.6% route share, a 16.9% target share, 2.11 YPRR, one deep target, and a 23.4% first-read share. Okonkwo could post another TE1 stat line this week. He's a strong streaming option. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the 11th-most yards per target to tight ends while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position.

Last week, Emanuel Wilson bounced back as the RB8 for the week. Wilson could easily lead the backfield again in touches this week, but we have to wait on Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price news. I'll update his outlook on Saturday.

Last week, Saquon Barkley finished as the RB20 for the week. This was impressive, as he had only nine touches that he turned into 71 total yards. He played only nine snaps while handling 28% of the rushing work and running two routes. Barkley can't be expected to run this hot on this limited amount of playing time weekly, despite his 15% explosive run rate, 2.42 yards after contact per attempt, and 23% missed tackle rate. Washington's run defense has also been strong. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the tenth-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the ninth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Dallas has been BLEEDING out production to the slot all season. Kendrick Bourne could be the next slot receiver to eat them alive this week. Since Week 5, Bourne has had one game with at least 12 PPR points while seeing a 15.3% target share with 1.45 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 16.7% first-read share. In their last five games, Dallas has allowed the most yards per target, the most receiving yards, and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers. Makai Lemon was the WR13 in weekly scoring last week against this defense.

Mark Andrews is the TE28 in fantasy points per game and hasn't had at least double-digit PPR points since Week 4. Andrews has a 66.1% route share, an 18.3% target share with 1.29 YPRR, five red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 20.5% first-read share. I have almost no confidence in Andrews at this point, but if you're desperate, he could have a mild bounce-back game this week. Across their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the fourth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. If he has a decent game, I won't be surprised, but I also won't be shocked if Andrews disappoints yet again against Buffalo.

Pat Freiermuth disappears against single-high. He has had two down games in a row with single-high heavy defenses on the menu, and he has another one this week. This week, he faces a Browns pass defense that has the highest single-high rate in the NFL (75.2%). Against single high, Freiermuth has a 13% TPRR with 0.77 YPRR. Sit Freiermuth this week.

Just when you think it's safe or advantageous to start Tyler Higbee, Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford pull the rug out from under you. After rattling off three straight awesome games, Higbee has stunk in the last two weeks. We have been forced to watch Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen soak up the tight end production for the Rams as we foolishly put Higbee into our lineups. Since Week 3, Higbee has had a 13.5% target share with 1.55 YPRR, two red zone targets, and a 16.1% first-read share. Over their last five games, the Bolts have limited tight ends to the fourth-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. This week, sit Higbee.

Courtland Sutton's fantasy value is non-existent. He is the WR70 in fantasy points per game without one game with at least double-digit PPR points. Sutton has a 14.2% target share with 0.94 YPRR, seven red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 21% first-read share. Sutton is a sit again this week. Across their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, Ja'Kobi Lane was second on the team with a 14.7% target share while having a 65% route share. Lane finished with 25 receiving yards (0.96 YPRR), two red zone targets, and a 15.4% first-read share (second on the team). Lane is a viable flex option this week. Over the last five weeks, Buffalo has allowed the second-most receiving fantasy points per game and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Aaron Jones sustained a knee injury in the fourth quarter last week. Jones will be back in the huddle this week. He didn't practice on Wednesday, but he had a limited session on Thursday and a full practice on Friday. He doesn't carry an injury designation into this week's game. Last week, in the first three quarters, Jones had a 35% snap rate, eight opportunities, 35% of the rushing work, and a 28.6% route share (5.3% target share). Jones has shown his age this season with only an 8.7% explosive run rate and a 12% missed tackle rate. I don't have high hopes for Jones this week, but if he gets in the end zone, he could be a decent flex. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the fifth-highest explosive run rate, the tenth-highest rushing success rate, and the sixth-most yards before contact per attempt.

Since Week 3, Michael Mayer has been the TE16 in fantasy points per game, with four weeks with at least 10.5 PPR points. During that span, he has had a 12.1% target share with 1.71 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 9.7% first-read share. The minimal touchdown equity and first-read share make Mayer a fringe streaming option only. In their last five games, New York has allowed the ninth-most yards per target to tight ends, but they have also held the position to only one receiving touchdown and the 14th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, Mason Taylor popped off with a two-touchdown performance and finished as the TE2 in weekly scoring behind only Trey McBride. Over the last two games, Taylor has had a 60.2% snap rate, a 56.1% route share, a 20% target share, 2.57 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 24.4% first-read share. He could keep the strong fantasy output going this week. Over the last five games, the Raiders have been hemorrhaging production to tight ends, giving up the second-most receiving fantasy points per game and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Taylor could be a TE1 again this week.
Tyler Warren missed last week's game with a groin injury. He opened this week with a limited practice. I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Over the last two games, Jake Ferguson's usage has been worrisome. Since Week 6, he has had a 54.1% snap rate, a 51.2% route share, a 4.9% target share, and only one first-read target. Yes, across their last five games, Arizona has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends, so Ferguson is on the fringe of streaming tight end options. I'm not starting him this week unless you truly are out of options, though.

Samaje Perine is a viable flex this week. Over the last two games, Perine has split the red zone work evenly with Chase Brown (two rushing attempts each) while averaging ten touches and 47 total yards. Perine has mustered a decent 10.3% explosive run rate and 2.29 yards after contact per attempt this season. Tennessee has fielded a putrid run defense recently. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards before contact per attempt. If Perine scores a touchdown with 10-12 touches this week, he could easily be a nice flex play.

Tyler Allgeier will split the workload with Jeremiyah Love this week. This season, he has had a 54.2% snap rate, 34.7% of the rushing work, and a 38.7% route share (5.4% target share). Allgeier has averaged 11 touches and 37.1 total yards. He has posted a solid 2.36 yards after contact per attempt and a disappointing 10% missed tackle rate. Allgeier should flirt with 10-12 touches this week as a decent flex play with a good matchup. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, J.K. Dobbins' role shrank as he finished with only six rushing attempts, 23 yards on the ground, and a touchdown. It was his lowest rushing attempt mark of the season while also having a season-low 23% snap rate. The Denver backfield seems to be shifting more in the direction of Jonah Coleman, which makes Dobbins a worrisome flex with a horrible matchup. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-lowest missed tackle rate. Sit Dobbins.

Darnell Washington has another single high matchup this week. Over the last two games, he has been the TE12 and TE23 in weekly scoring with touchdowns in both games. In those games, he has had a 64% snap rate, a 36.4% route share, a 7.6% target share, 0.91 YPRR, three red zone targets, and an 8% first-read share. This week, he faces a Browns pass defense that has the highest single high rate in the NFL (75.2%). Against single high, Washington has had a 23% TPRR with 1.78 YPRR. Washington is a viable streaming option this week. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends.

Since Week 6, TreVeyon Henderson has continued to operate as Rhamondre Stevenson's change of pace with a 23.8% snap rate, 6.5 touches, and 31.5 total yards per game. Henderson is only a dart-throw flex with a good matchup. Henderson's rushing efficiency continues to be non-existent with only 1.79 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate, but we know his home run speed is real. If he gets a crease, he can take any carry to the house. If you're flexing him this week, this is exactly what you're hoping for. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt, the seventh-highest gap yards per carry, and the sixth-highest gap rushing success rate (Henderson: 65.4% gap). Henderson is dealing with an illness. He missed practice on Thursday and Friday. He has been listed as questionable. Monitor his status on Sunday.

Last week, in his first game back from the finger injury, Adonai Mitchell had only a 51.5% route share, a 10% target share, and a 15% first-read share. He's a sit this week and until further notice, until we see his playing time jump back into a full-time starting workload. That could be this week, but it's impossible to know and not worth the risk in Week 8.
Tre Harris opened this week with a limited practice (hamstring). I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Last week, Chris Bell had only a 53.6% route share and 48.4% snap rate with Caleb Douglas back and Malik Washington in the lineup. We need to see Chris Bell's usage bounce back with Douglas back in the lineup before putting him into a fantasy lineup.

Brian Thomas Jr.'s only hope this season seems to be a trade at this point. Over the last two games, he has played only 51.4% and 21.1% of the snaps while drawing a total of five targets (zero receptions). He's not startable for fantasy purposes until something changes.

Rashee Rice will be back this week (hamstring). He opened the week with limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. He had a full practice on Friday. Rice doesn't carry an injury designation into this week. In Weeks 1-3, Rice was the WR23 in fantasy points per game. He had a 16.3% target share with 2.35 YPRR, four red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 20.3% first-read share. Rice will have a long day this week. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the 14th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. They will also get Patrick Surtain back. If you're forced to start Rice, I get it, but temper your expectations this week.
